What is the Wolfram Language and how is evaluation structured?

The Wolfram Language (WL) is the programming language behind Mathematica, Wolfram Alpha, and the Wolfram Cloud. It is symbolic, functional, and rule-based — every expression is a symbolic term; computation is rewriting.

**Key insight**: all expressions have the form `Head[arg1, arg2, ...]`

```wolfram
Head[1 + 2]         (* Plus *)
Head["hello"]       (* String *)
Head[{1, 2, 3}]    (* List *)
Head[Sin[x]]        (* Sin *)
FullForm[1 + 2*x]  (* Plus[1, Times[2, x]] *)
```

```wolfram
(* Tools *)
Print["Hello, World!"]
(* wolframscript -code 'Print["Hello"]' *)
(* wolframscript -file hello.wl *)
```

**Evaluation model**: WL repeatedly rewrites expressions using built-in and user-defined rules until no rule applies.

How do variables, assignment, arithmetic, and exact computation work in Wolfram Language?

```wolfram
(* Variables and assignment *)
x = 42
y = Pi               (* symbolic — not 3.14159 *)
name = "Alice"
Clear[x, y, name]   (* clear bindings *)

(* := delayed assignment — evaluated each time *)
f[n_] := n^2 + 1
rand := RandomReal[]  (* fresh random each time *)

(* Arithmetic — EXACT by default! *)
10 / 3              (* 10/3 — exact fraction! *)
N[10/3]             (* 3.33333... — numerical *)
N[Pi, 50]           (* Pi to 50 digits *)
2^100               (* exact: 1267650600228229401496703205376 *)
Mod[17, 5]          (* 2 *)
GCD[12, 8]          (* 4 *)
Factorial[10]       (* 3628800 *)
Binomial[10, 3]     (* 120 *)
Fibonacci[20]       (* 6765 *)
PrimeQ[17]          (* True *)
Prime[100]          (* 541 — 100th prime *)

(* Type checks *)
IntegerQ[42]        (* True *)
NumberQ[3.14]       (* True *)
StringQ["hi"]       (* True *)
ListQ[{1,2,3}]     (* True *)
AtomQ[42]          (* True — cannot be broken down *)
AtomQ[f[x]]        (* False *)
```

How do lists and functional operations work in Wolfram Language?

```wolfram
(* Lists — fundamental data structure *)
list = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
Length[list]           (* 5 *)
First[list]            (* 1 *)
Last[list]             (* 5 *)
Rest[list]             (* {2, 3, 4, 5} *)
Most[list]             (* {1, 2, 3, 4} *)
list[[1]]              (* 1 — 1-indexed! *)
list[[2;;4]]           (* {2, 3, 4} — span *)
list[[-1]]             (* 5 — last element *)

(* Creating lists *)
Range[5]               (* {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} *)
Range[0, 10, 2]        (* {0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10} *)
Table[i^2, {i, 1, 10}] (* {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...} *)
ConstantArray[0, 5]    (* {0, 0, 0, 0, 0} *)

(* Modifying *)
Append[list, 6]        (* {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} — non-destructive *)
Prepend[list, 0]
Join[{1,2}, {3,4}]    (* {1, 2, 3, 4} *)
Reverse[list]
Sort[{3,1,4,1,5}]     (* {1, 1, 3, 4, 5} *)
Union[{1,2,2,3}]       (* {1, 2, 3} — unique+sorted *)

(* Functional operations *)
Map[f, {1,2,3}]               (* {f[1], f[2], f[3]} *)
Map[#^2 &, {1,2,3}]           (* {1, 4, 9} *)
{1,2,3,4,5} /@ (# * 2 &)     (* {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} — shorthand Map *)
Select[Range[10], EvenQ]       (* {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} *)
Fold[Plus, 0, {1,2,3,4,5}]   (* 15 *)
FoldList[Plus, 0, {1,2,3}]   (* {0, 1, 3, 6} *)
Apply[Plus, list]              (* 15 = Plus @@ list *)
Total[list]                    (* 15 *)
```

How does pattern matching and rule application work in Wolfram Language?

```wolfram
(* Pattern types *)
_          (* any single expression (blank) *)
__         (* any sequence of 1+ expressions *)
___        (* any sequence of 0+ expressions *)
_h         (* any expression with head h *)
x_         (* any expression, bound to x *)
x_Integer  (* any integer, bound to x *)
x_ /; x > 0  (* any positive number *)

(* Testing patterns *)
MatchQ[3, _Integer]         (* True *)
MatchQ[{1,2,3}, {__Integer}] (* True *)
MatchQ[f[x,y], f[_,_]]     (* True *)

(* Replace rules *)
x^2 + y /. x -> 3              (* 9 + y *)
x^2 + y /. {x -> 3, y -> 1}   (* 10 *)
{1,2,3,4,5} /. n_ /; n > 3 -> 0  (* {1,2,3,0,0} *)
x^2 + x + 1 /. x^n_ -> a^n    (* a^2 + a + 1 *)

(* Replace repeatedly (//.  — until fixed point) *)
{1,2,3} //. x:{a___,b_,c_,d___} /; b > c :> {a,c,b,d}
(* sorts the list! *)

(* Rules as data *)
rules = {a -> 1, b -> 2, c -> 3}
a + b + c /. rules   (* 6 *)

(* Function definitions use patterns *)
f[0] = 1
f[n_Integer /; n > 0] := n * f[n-1]
f[5]   (* 120 *)

(* Default values *)
h[x_, y_:0] := x + y   (* y defaults to 0 *)
h[3]        (* 3 *)
h[3, 4]     (* 7 *)
```

How does calculus and algebra work in Wolfram Language?

```wolfram
(* Derivatives *)
D[Sin[x], x]              (* Cos[x] *)
D[x^3 + 2x^2 - x, x]    (* 3x^2 + 4x - 1 *)
D[f[x], {x, 2}]          (* f''[x] — second derivative *)
D[x*y^2 + z, y]          (* 2xy — partial *)

(* Integration *)
Integrate[x^2, x]          (* x^3/3 *)
Integrate[Sin[x], {x, 0, Pi}]  (* 2 *)
Integrate[Exp[-x^2], {x, -Infinity, Infinity}]  (* Sqrt[Pi] *)

(* Limits, series, sums *)
Limit[Sin[x]/x, x -> 0]    (* 1 *)
Limit[(1 + 1/n)^n, n -> Infinity]  (* E *)
Series[Sin[x], {x, 0, 7}]  (* Taylor series *)
Sum[n^2, {n, 1, 10}]       (* 385 *)
Sum[1/n^2, {n, 1, Infinity}]  (* Pi^2/6 *)
Product[n, {n, 1, 10}]    (* 3628800 *)

(* Algebra *)
Expand[(x + y)^3]
Factor[x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x - 1]   (* (x-1)^3 *)
Simplify[(x^2 - 1)/(x - 1)]    (* 1 + x *)
Together[(1/x + 1/y)]           (* (x+y)/(xy) *)
Apart[(x^2+1)/(x*(x-1))]       (* partial fractions *)

(* Solving equations *)
Solve[x^2 - 5x + 6 == 0, x]    (* {{x->2},{x->3}} *)
NSolve[x^3 - x - 2 == 0, x]    (* numerical *)
Reduce[x^2 < 9, x]              (* -3 < x < 3 *)
FindRoot[Cos[x] == x, {x, 0.5}]  (* {x -> 0.739085} *)

(* Differential equations *)
DSolve[y'[x] == y[x], y, x]   (* {{y->C[1]*E^x}} *)
NDSolve[{y'[x] == -2*y[x], y[0] == 1}, y, {x, 0, 5}]
```

How does graphics and visualization work in Wolfram Language?

```wolfram
(* 2D plotting *)
Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 2Pi}]
Plot[{Sin[x], Cos[x]}, {x, 0, 2Pi}]
Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 2Pi},
    PlotStyle -> {Thick, Blue},
    AxesLabel -> {"x", "sin(x)"},
    PlotLabel -> "Sine Wave"]

(* Parametric and data *)
ParametricPlot[{Sin[t], Cos[t]}, {t, 0, 2Pi}]
ParametricPlot[{t*Cos[t], t*Sin[t]}, {t, 0, 4Pi}]  (* spiral *)
ListPlot[{1, 4, 9, 16, 25}]
ListLinePlot[{1, 4, 9, 16, 25}]

(* 3D plotting *)
Plot3D[Sin[x*y], {x, -Pi, Pi}, {y, -Pi, Pi}]
Plot3D[Sin[x]*Cos[y], {x, -Pi, Pi}, {y, -Pi, Pi},
    ColorFunction -> "Rainbow",
    PlotPoints -> 50]
ContourPlot[x^2 + y^2, {x, -2, 2}, {y, -2, 2}]

(* Statistical plots *)
Histogram[RandomReal[{0, 1}, 1000]]
BarChart[{3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9}]
PieChart[{30, 25, 45}]

(* Multiple plots *)
Show[
    Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 2Pi}],
    Plot[Cos[x], {x, 0, 2Pi}]
]

(* Export *)
Export["plot.png", Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 2Pi}]]
Export["plot.pdf", plot]
```

How does functional programming work in Wolfram Language? Show pure functions, composition, and Nest.

```wolfram
(* Pure functions (Function or & shorthand) *)
Function[x, x^2][5]    (* 25 *)
(#^2 &)[5]             (* 25 — shorthand *)
(#1 + #2 &)[3, 4]      (* 7 — named slots *)

(* Composition *)
Composition[f, g, h][x]   (* f[g[h[x]]] *)
(f @* g @* h)[x]          (* same — @* is Composition *)

(* Repeated application *)
Nest[f, x, 3]           (* f[f[f[x]]] *)
NestList[f, x, 3]       (* {x, f[x], f[f[x]], f[f[f[x]]]} *)
NestWhile[#*2 &, 1, # < 100 &]  (* 128 — double while < 100 *)
FixedPoint[Cos, 1.0]    (* 0.739085... — iterate until stable *)
FixedPointList[Cos, 1.0]

(* Map variants *)
f /@ {1,2,3}            (* Map: {f[1],f[2],f[3]} *)
f @@@ {{1,2},{3,4}}     (* Apply at level 1: {f[1,2],f[3,4]} *)
{1,2,3} // f            (* Postfix: f[{1,2,3}] *)

(* Thread (like Map but for multiple lists) *)
Thread[f[{1,2,3}, {a,b,c}]]  (* {f[1,a], f[2,b], f[3,c]} *)
MapThread[f, {{1,2,3},{a,b,c}}]  (* same *)

(* Reap/Sow — collect values during computation *)
{result, collected} = Reap[
    Do[Sow[i^2], {i, 1, 5}]
]
(* collected = {{1,4,9,16,25}} *)

(* Scan (Map for side effects) *)
Scan[Print, {1, 2, 3}]   (* prints 1, 2, 3 *)
```

How do Associations (dictionaries), string operations, and control flow work in Wolfram Language?

```wolfram
(* Association — key-value structure *)
assoc = <|"name" -> "Alice", "age" -> 30, "city" -> "NYC"|>
assoc["name"]              (* "Alice" *)
assoc[["age"]]             (* 30 — part notation *)
KeyExistsQ[assoc, "name"]  (* True *)
Keys[assoc]                (* {"name","age","city"} *)
Values[assoc]
KeyTake[assoc, {"name","age"}]
KeyDrop[assoc, {"city"}]
Map[# + 1 &, <|a->1, b->2|>]    (* <|a->2, b->3|> *)
Merge[{<|a->1|>, <|a->2, b->3|>}, Total]  (* <|a->3, b->3|> *)

(* String operations *)
StringLength["hello"]              (* 5 *)
ToUpperCase["hello"]               (* "HELLO" *)
StringTake["hello world", 5]       (* "hello" *)
StringJoin["Hello", ", ", "World!"] (* "Hello, World!" *)
StringReplace["hello", "l" -> "L"]  (* "heLLo" *)
StringSplit["a,b,c", ","]           (* {"a","b","c"} *)
StringContainsQ["hello", "ell"]     (* True *)
StringMatchQ["hello", "h" ~~ __ ~~ "o"]  (* True *)
StringCases["phone: 555-1234", DigitCharacter..]  (* {"555","1234"} *)

(* Control flow *)
If[condition, t, f]
Which[c1, v1, c2, v2, True, default]
Switch[val, p1, v1, p2, v2, _, default]

(* Loops *)
Do[Print[i], {i, 1, 5}]               (* 1 to 5 *)
Do[Print[i], {i, 1, 10, 2}]           (* step 2 *)
Do[f[i, j], {i, 1, 3}, {j, 1, 3}]    (* nested *)
While[n > 0, n -= 1]
For[i = 0, i < 10, i++, Print[i]]

(* Module — local variables *)
Module[{x = 10, y = 20},
    x^2 + y^2]   (* 500 *)

(* Block — temporarily override globals *)
x = 5;
Block[{x = 100}, x^2]   (* 10000, x is 5 again after *)

(* With — substitution *)
With[{n = 42}, n^2 + n]   (* 1806 *)
```
